content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It uses only es-toolkit and no lodash import, and it type-checks cleanly. Its bundle measures 2364 bytes (min+gzip) with 97 bytes of own code.

```ts
import { merge } from 'es-toolkit';
import { startCase, truncate } from 'es-toolkit/compat';
```

- **`applyPatch`** uses root `merge`. It matches lodash's index-wise array merge and mutates `base` the same way. On 20,000 random in-range cases it matched the compat `merge`, which is documented as lodash-compatible.
- **`toTitle`** uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The root `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so `"ID"` would become `"Id"`, while lodash keeps `"ID"`. The compat version keeps case, as lodash does.
- **`preview`** uses `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`. Root es-toolkit doesn't export `truncate`. The compat version takes lodash's `{ length }` options shape, so no adapter was needed. It returns strings of length 24 or less unchanged and truncates longer ones to 21 characters plus `...`, as lodash does.

I didn't use the all-compat variant (`merge`, `startCase`, `truncate` all from `es-toolkit/compat`). It measured 4044 bytes gzipped against 2364 for the chosen version. The compat `merge` pulls in a lot of extra code that root `merge` avoids.

Things to be aware of:

- **Lodash isn't installed here, so I couldn't compare against the original directly.** The original `src/module.ts` fails to type-check and can't be bundled in this checkout.
